details: Bitcoin saw a modest rebound to around $60,474 on November 23, recovering from a weekend low near $55,500. However, this minor recovery occurred despite significant selling pressure in the broader crypto market. U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded substantial net outflows of $569.7 million on November 23 alone, contributing to a record $4.71 billion in total outflows for November. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index remains at an "extreme fear" level of 11, indicating widespread investor caution.
title: Crypto Market Rebounds Slightly Amid Record ETF Outflows

details: The upcoming October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation report, scheduled for release on November 25, is a key focus for markets. Forecasts suggest the annual core PCE inflation will rise to 3.2%, up from 3.1% in September, remaining above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. On November 23, New York Fed President John C. Williams reiterated that while the economy shows resilience, inflation is "simply too high," underscoring the Federal Reserve's commitment to further actions to bring inflation down. The advance estimate for Q3 GDP also showed strong growth of 3.4% annually.
sourceName: TIOmarkets & Federal Reserve Bank of New York
title: US Inflation Expected to Rise as Fed Maintains Hawkish Stance

details: Global equity markets experienced significant volatility and sell-offs last week, particularly in technology and AI-linked stocks. The S&P 500 entered correction territory, and the Nasdaq recorded its worst weekly decline since March 2020. This "AI unwind" is attributed to investors re-evaluating the profitability and long-term returns on the substantial investments made in Artificial Intelligence infrastructure. Despite underlying demand for AI technology, market sentiment is shifting from enthusiasm to a more disciplined assessment of AI business models, leading to near-term volatility.
title: AI Sector Volatility Fuels Broader Equity Market Sell-Off
